speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. Can you tell me how long you've noticed the swelling and pain in your right ring finger, and did it start after any specific injury or event?

speaker: Patient
text: 22-year-old male. The patient reports that the pain and swelling in his right ring finger began 2 days ago while playing football. He recalls his finger got caught in the jersey of another player, who then pulled away forcefully.

speaker: Doctor
text: Can you describe the type of pain you're feeling, and is the finger currently unable to bend straight or curl fully? Also, do you notice any bruising or a visible deformity?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Progressive swelling and pain in the right ring finger. I also have Inability to flex the right ring finger at the distal interphalangeal joint when making a fist, Pain at the distal interphalangeal joint, Extended right ring finger in resting position.

speaker: Doctor
text:
That inability to flex the fingertip, combined with the finger staying extended at rest, is highly suggestive of a "mallet finger" injury to the extensor tendon. Do you feel any sharp pain when I gently try to pull the fingertip into a bent position?

REQUEST TEST: Right Ring Finger X-Ray

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: X-ray of the Right Hand: No bone fractures or dislocations visible. Soft tissue swelling noted around the distal interphalangeal joint of the right ring finger.

speaker: Doctor
text: Since the X-ray rules out a fracture, this appears to be a soft tissue injury specifically involving the extensor tendon. Can you confirm if there is any numbness or tingling in the finger, and have you tried applying ice or keeping the joint straight since the injury?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: No significant medical history. Social history: Student and active in sports, particularly football. Non-smoker and drinks alcohol socially.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the history; given the mechanism and the inability to flex the distal joint without fracture, this confirms a soft tissue mallet finger. I have enough information to finalize my assessment. DIAGNOSIS READY: Mallet Finger (Avulsion of the Extensor Tendon Insertion)

DIAGNOSIS_READY_Answer: Rupture of the flexor digitorum profundus tendon at its point of insertion
